findings.title: Samsung Securities Also Hit by Hack: Personal Data of 8,241 VOC Submitters Leaked
findings.summary_md: The Asia Business Daily reported that Samsung Securities posted a press release and customer apology on 23 November after detecting an external intrusion into its Voice of Customer system on 21 November. The report says 8,241 customers were affected and that 13 categories of data, including names, account numbers, addresses, contact details and driver's license numbers, were involved, varying by customer. It says the company blocked the attack with its firewall, notified the Financial Supervisory Service and KISA, and told customers that only VOC submitters were in scope.

findings.title: 삼성증권, VOC 시스템 해킹…8241명 개인정보 유출
findings.summary_md: Digital Times reported that Samsung Securities found external intrusion traces in its VOC system on 21 November and confirmed that some attachments uploaded by customers had been exported. It says 8,241 customers were affected, with 13 possible data fields including names, account numbers, addresses, contact details and driver's license numbers; the exact fields differ by person. The article says the company blocked the attacking IP, suspended the service, reported to the Financial Supervisory Service and KISA, and warned of voice phishing, spam and malware follow-on risk.

findings.title: [속보] 삼성증권 ‘고객의 소리’ 해킹…8241명 개인정보 13개항목 유출
findings.summary_md: Kyunghyang Shinmun reported Samsung Securities' customer apology stating that an unauthorized external party accessed the VOC intake service on the afternoon of 21 November and that some customer-uploaded attachments were leaked. It puts the victim count at 8,241 and lists 13 personal-data categories including names, account numbers, addresses, contact details and driver's license numbers, with the precise set varying by customer. The report says the company blocked the IP, suspended the service, checked other systems and reported the incident to regulators.

findings.title: (LEAD) Personal information of more than 8,000 clients at Samsung Securities breached
findings.summary_md: Yonhap reported that Samsung Securities said personal data of more than 8,000 clients had been breached in what it called the latest cyberattack on South Korean financial firms. The brokerage said unauthorized access was detected on its customer response website on Saturday and that customer names, physical addresses and other personal information were compromised. Yonhap says the breach did not extend beyond the affected system and that Samsung reported the incident to authorities and said it was strengthening its cybersecurity systems.
